text:
Blake Coleman is 34, won two Stanley Cups with Tampa Bay, and is 25 games into his first season with the Wild after 392 in Calgary. He's playing the way he always has: 46 hits, penalty killing, and shots from close in. His own chances are up, 1.16 expected goals per 60 (the quality of his chances) against 1.00 last season.

Minnesota has been winning, and he's part of it: 8 points in his last ten games, ahead of the 5.2 we'd expect at his ice time, including three points against Boston. Some of that is on-ice bounces, with the Wild scoring 3.9 more goals than expected while he's out there. His own goals, 7 on 7.7 expected, are right where they should be.

Evolving-Hockey had him 1.9 wins above replacement last season, 58th among 401 forwards, and in the 96th percentile for taking chances away. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the offensive side: 87th percentile for chances from in front of the net. Watch him on the penalty kill and around the crease. That's where he earns his minutes.
headline: Blake Coleman brings his usual work to Minnesota
